a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every N of type S1 X Y there exists an N' of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N' has at least one index, and for every ordered pair of its indices m and n there is a directed chain of one or more steps from m to n. A step from i to j means that there exist two state assignments for N' and an input x in X such that the assignments agree at every index other than i, but the update at j gives different values for those assignments with the same input x. The assignments need not be reachable. The chain requirement includes m = n, so each index must have a positive-length chain back to itself. (2) N' has exactly as many indices as N; the index types need not be identical. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N' and N give equal outputs when each starts from its own initial assignment, processes the list from left to right, and applies its own output function. Their internal states need not agree. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or on the index type of N. In particular, N with zero indices is not excluded, even though in that case conditions (1) and (2) are incompatible."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every pair of types X and Y, if X is nonempty, then for every N of type S1 X Y there exists an N' of type S1 X Y satisfying all three conditions: (1) N' has at least one index, and for every ordered pair of its indices m and n there is a directed chain of one or more steps from m to n. A step from i to j means that there exist two state assignments for N' and an input x in X such that the assignments agree at every index other than i, but the update at j gives different values for those assignments with the same input x. The assignments need not be reachable. The chain requirement includes m = n, so each index must have a positive-length chain back to itself. (2) N' has exactly as many indices as N; the index types need not be identical. (3) For every finite list of inputs from X, including the empty list and with no length bound, N' and N give equal outputs when each starts from its own initial assignment, processes the list from left to right, and applies its own output function. Their internal states need not agree. There is no separate nonemptiness hypothesis on Y or on the index type of N. In particular, N with zero indices is not excluded, even though in that case conditions (1) and (2) are incompatible.

divergences.description: The TARGET requires `N'.d13 = N.d13` (the same number of units), not `N'.d13 = N.d13 + 1`. This makes the proposition false for an allowed zero-unit system: the equality forces the twin to have zero units, but `N'.D11` requires at least one.

judgement.summary: The input hypothesis, structural feedback condition and equality of outputs after every finite history otherwise match the description. The passage comparison is apt as a model-specific one: P2’s converse requires equal input-output functions without specifying a history domain or time limit, and Appendix A preserves F(x) while allowing arbitrarily high ϕ.
